subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default safety policy should OpenClaw enforce for cron jobs registered by plugins or external tools?
rationale: The fix changes public cron/plugin behavior, upgrade defaults, model-cost policy, and security provenance; source inspection proves the gap but not the intended product contract.

options.title: Require explicit activation for external/plugin crons
options.body: Default third-party/plugin-created recurring model-backed jobs to disabled or pending, surface them in doctor/update, and require a user action before they run.

options.title: Keep activation but add warnings and budgets
options.body: Preserve current enabled behavior while adding model-cost warnings, dry-run summaries, and quota circuit breakers to reduce spend risk with lower compatibility impact.

options.title: Split into narrow tracked work
options.body: Keep this issue as the consent/provenance canonical item and route circuit breakers and budgets to the existing related issues.

recommendation.title: Require explicit activation for external/plugin crons
recommendation.body: Default third-party/plugin-created recurring model-backed jobs to disabled or pending, surface them in doctor/update, and require a user action before they run.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is on both cron service behavior and the plugin scheduled-turn bridge that reproduces the issue.
